discovery: The electron recollision (three-step) model of strong-field physics, the theoretical foundation of high-harmonic generation and attosecond science

nominees.name: Paul B. Corkum
nominees.affiliation: University of Ottawa and National Research Council Canada

nominees.name: Maciej Lewenstein
nominees.affiliation: ICFO - Institut de Ciencies Fotoniques, Barcelona

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics: strong-field and attosecond physics
motivation: In 1993 Corkum, and Schafer with co-workers, showed that an electron tunnel-ionized by an intense laser field is driven back to its parent ion, where it can recombine, scatter or eject further electrons. Lewenstein and co-workers turned this picture into a quantitative quantum theory (the strong-field approximation for harmonic generation) that remains the working framework of the field. Recollision explained the harmonic plateau and its cutoff, nonsequential double ionization and laser-induced electron diffraction, and Corkum then showed how to exploit it to produce and measure attosecond pulses and to image orbitals. The 2023 prize honoured experimental methods for attosecond pulses; the conceptual and theoretical insight that made those methods possible and interpretable has not yet been recognised. Every modern attosecond experiment, in atoms, molecules and now solids, is designed and read through this model. It is a rare case of simple, predictive theory reshaping an entire field.
